metadata.description: Code and machine-checked formal verification for the paper "Forecasting Processes That Are Not Sequences: What Flattening Costs Object-Centric Process Model Forecasting". Every figure and table in the paper regenerates from a single command (bash experiments/run_all.sh). Six stages run end to end: verification of the formal layer against the same implementation the experiments use, a checksummed fetch of the event logs, 36 invariant and golden-file tests, series construction, the flat-versus-object-centric benchmark, the calibration arm, and the tables and figures. Each stage writes a manifest recording the seed, the configuration hash, the code commit and the library versions. They are fetched at run time from Zenodo record 8433706 and verified against the checksums that record declares. They remain CC BY 4.0 by their original authors. Environment of record: Python 3.12.13, numpy 2.2.6, seed 42, macOS arm64. Exact pins in requirements.txt.

metadata.title: Artifacts of Evaluating Shaker for Flaky Test Detection in Python Projects
metadata.description:
Replication package for the paper "Evaluating Shaker for Flaky Test Detection in Python Projects", published at SAST 2026, the 11th Brazilian Symposium on Systematic and Automated Software Testing.

The paper evaluates Shaker, a flaky-test detector that injects CPU and memory stress to amplify non-determinism, on Python for the first time. It compares Shaker against a budget-matched plain re-execution baseline ("ReRun") on 137 ground-truth flaky tests taken from the dataset of Gruber et al., and reports a null result: at an equal budget of 100 executions per test, stress injection detects no more flaky tests than simply rerunning them (37.2% against 35.8%, McNemar exact p = 0.84). Fewer than half of the ground-truth tests reproduced on independent hardware at all (45.3%), and those that did are dominated by randomness and network flakiness rather than the concurrency Shaker targets.

CONTENTS

analysis/    Scripts that rebuild every table and figure in the paper from the shipped result CSVs.
experiment/  Docker orchestration runner and results parser used to execute the study.
docker/      Two images: one for the analysis, one for test execution under stress.
shaker_py/   The Shaker tool, modified for this study. See shaker_py/NOTICE for the exact changes.
dataset/     Study inputs: ground truth, manual flakiness labels, project list, runner inputs.
results/     The two parsed result CSVs behind the paper's numbers.
raw_results/ A partial snapshot of the raw per-test output trees.
paper.pdf    The accepted paper.

REPRODUCING THE PAPER

With Docker installed, running ./run_analysis.sh from the root of the artifact rebuilds every table and figure of the paper into ./output/. It takes about a minute, needs no Python on the host, executes no tests, and requires no network access at run time. A plain Python virtualenv route producing byte-identical output is documented as well.

The expected headline numbers are Shaker 51/137 (37.2%), ReRun 49/137 (35.8%), McNemar exact p = 0.839, which are the values reported in the paper's abstract and in Table 1.

The README also documents the optional path that re-runs the experiments themselves, in isolated Docker containers under Shaker's stress and under the ReRun baseline. That path takes days of compute and saturates the host machine by design.

REQUIREMENTS

For the analysis, either Docker alone, or Python 3.10 or newer with scipy, pandas, and matplotlib. Roughly 50 MB of disk for the artifact and 550 MB for the analysis image. Re-running the experiments additionally needs a Docker daemon, network access, and several GB of disk.

DATA AND ETHICS

The artifact contains no personal, human-subject, or otherwise sensitive data. All data are execution metadata (pass/fail verdicts, run counts, and repository size metrics) for the automated test suites of publicly available open-source Python packages published on PyPI. The subject projects are not redistributed: the experiment clones each one from its own public repository at the commit recorded in dataset/projects.csv, and each remains under its own licence.

LICENSING

Code (analysis/, experiment/, docker/, shaker_py/, and the shell scripts) is released under the BSD 2-Clause License. Data (dataset/, results/, raw_results/) is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, matching the licence of the dataset of Gruber et al. from which the ground-truth files derive. See the LICENSE file at the root of the artifact for the full text, the scope of each licence, and the third-party attributions.

RELATED RESOURCES

Development repository: https://github.com/STAR-RG/shaker-python-sast2026
Upstream Shaker: https://github.com/STAR-RG/shaker and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5347973
Ground-truth dataset of Gruber et al.: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4450435

metadata.title: Reproducibility Package for Fuzhao: A Comprehensively Optimal Traditional Randomization Protocol and Its Exact Compilation System
metadata.description:
This record contains the frozen computational artifact accompanying the publication Fuzhao: A Comprehensively Optimal Traditional Randomization Protocol and Its Exact Compilation System. Version 1.0.0 preserves the exact protocol, experiment source, historical-source records, bounded-priority search records, deterministic scientific outputs, mathematical registries, evidence indexes, release bindings, and executable verification programs required to inspect and reconstruct the claims reported in the publication.

Reproduction architecture

The package separates source construction, exact compilation, target-specific lower-bound calculation, canonical decoding, matched-source comparison, fixed-binary source-frontier evaluation, compact-decoder auditing, boundary validation, historical-priority screening, and implementation verification.

Primary claims are evaluated with exhaustive finite populations or exact integer arithmetic. The complete source bijection, Fu and Zhao laws, uniform-index compilers, direct target trees, fixed-position binary frontier, compact common-Dayan decoder, bias and noise boundaries, and nonidentifiability cases are each preserved as canonical machine-readable outputs. Independently seeded Monte Carlo sampling is retained only as an implementation-path check.

The primary intersection-union claim contains seven retained experimental components. Historical priority is evaluated separately against a sealed Chinese- and English-language search protocol, query-result log, and candidate registry. The registry records four eligibility gates and five grouped performance fields. Target-specific source-depth optimality and matched-seven strict advantage each contain two prespecified endpoints, yielding seven counted performance components.

Data and evidence binding

All generated scientific outputs are reconstructed from the frozen protocol and the released experiment source. No learned, fitted, or generative model is used.

results/results_index.json is the primary machine-readable navigation index for the canonical scientific outputs. results/paper_numbers.json records the exact values reported in the publication. formula_audit.json and math_registry.json preserve the mathematical audit layer.

frozen/frozen_protocol.json fixes the source models, target laws, complete populations, seeds, budgets, endpoints, comparators, multiplicity rules, retention rules, boundary regimes, and historical component-counting rule. frozen/preexecution_freeze.json and frozen/freeze_manifest.json bind the protocol, source, and search records fixed before execution.

sources/historical_search_protocol.json records the bounded historical-priority search. sources/historical_candidate_registry.csv records the candidate screen. sources/historical_search_log.csv records the retained query-result pairs, candidate mappings, and dispositions. Source-specific records preserve the cited Hacker, Patton, Wu, and Cottrell materials.

sources/companion_publications.json records the two ISBN-bearing companion method editions and their SHA-256 fingerprints. The companion PDFs are distributed beside the package and are not duplicated inside the ZIP.

release/release_binding.json binds the frozen protocol, experiment source, source and search records, canonical result index, released publication PDF, and both companion method editions to version 1.0.0.

manifest.json records the SHA-256 digest and byte size of every tracked package file other than itself.

Verification and execution scope

The root package verifier checks package identifiers, tracked file sizes and SHA-256 digests, frozen-input bindings, release identifiers, result-index bindings, historical gate and component counts, required screened candidates, UTF-8/LF normalization, cache exclusion, unsafe paths, and possible embedded credentials.

The reproduction verifier reruns the frozen experiment program under the required Python and NumPy versions, regenerates the indexed scientific results in a clean temporary directory, and compares the canonical outputs byte for byte. Execution metadata are validated semantically because machine identity and elapsed time are environment dependent.

The package contains separate evidence for complete-source capacity, exact traditional three-coin and common-Dayan compilation, source-relative decision-tree optimality, the fixed-position binary source frontier, the compact table-free common-Dayan decoder, boundary stress, protocol equivalence, bias and read-noise transfer, nonidentifiability, historical configuration comparison, bounded historical priority, and independently seeded Monte Carlo verification.

Release integrity

The external SHA256SUMS file records the final publication PDF, the two companion publications, and the standalone reproducibility-package ZIP. Its SHA-256 digest is sealed by an RFC 3161 trusted timestamp issued at 2026-08-26 17:31:35 UTC. The timestamped message imprint exactly equals the SHA-256 digest of the released SHA256SUMS file.

The package excludes unrelated development trials, caches, credentials, private material, DOCX files, DOCX fingerprints, and machine-specific absolute paths. Scientific text files use UTF-8 without BOM and LF newlines.

Fuzhao-authored code, experiment material, evidence records, and documentation are licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

metadata.title: Evidence Ledger MVP: Blockchain-Based Digital Evidence Certification Platform
metadata.description:
Evidence Ledger MVP is a research artifact developed under the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology.
 
The platform provides cryptographic certification, indexing, traceability, integrity verification and auditing of digital evidence through SHA-256 hashing and a blockchain-inspired ledger architecture.
 
The solution was designed to support governance, compliance, auditing, risk management and digital evidence preservation processes. It was conceived as a complementary digital trust layer, allowing organizations to verify the integrity and traceability of digital evidence while preserving original documents in existing repositories.
 
Main features:
 
• SHA-256 hash generation
• Digital evidence certification
• Evidence integrity verification
• Blockchain-inspired ledger registration
• Audit trail generation
• SQLite FTS5 indexing
• REST API integration
• RPA integration capability
• Offline-first architecture
 
The repository contains source code, technical documentation, user manuals, sample datasets, validation materials and reproducibility artifacts required to reproduce the experiments associated with the research.
 
The artifact was developed as part of an MBA research project focused on strengthening the integrity, traceability and auditability of digital evidence used in internal control, compliance and governance environments.

metadata.title: CollocAgent: A Corpus-Grounded System for Auditable Collocation Feedback
metadata.description:
CollocAgent is a standalone system for collocation feedback in second-language
academic writing. It separates the task into three components with an explicit
evidence boundary: a diagnostic component that locates a candidate span and
assigns a construction type and severity, a retrieval component that queries a
local corpus index and ranks replacement candidates by attestation, within-window
pair frequency and log-Dice, and an explanation component that may only report
values produced by retrieval.

Every result carries a provenance record containing the corpus name, the
co-occurrence window, the token and sentence counts, the retrieved counts and a
SHA-256 fingerprint of the indexed source files. When the index contains no
support for a recommendation, the system returns an explicit insufficient-evidence
status instead of a number.

The implementation uses only the Python standard library, requires Python 3.10 or
later, and runs from a command-line interface, a local JSON API and a browser
client. Container files are included.

Verification of this release: nine unit tests passed, and ten constructed fixtures
were each detected with the expected top-ranked candidate. These are software
checks establishing that the components execute as specified. They are not a
linguistic evaluation, and no precision, recall, F-score, hallucination rate or
human rating is claimed. The bundled corpus is synthetic and exists only to verify
execution; no licensed corpus text or frequency table is included.

This deposit contains the software artifact only.
